economy.summary: His campaign says he has pushed to enact pro-growth policies that would enable the private sector to protect and create family-sustaining jobs, and that he authored legislation to make it easier for veterans to get jobs in the private sector.
economy.short: Says he pushes pro-growth policies and veteran jobs legislation.

taxes.summary: Voted for the 2025-26 state budget, calling it a return to responsible governing; he cited a new tax credit program for low- to moderate-income working families and tightened eligibility verification for public assistance programs.
taxes.short: Voted for 2025-26 budget; cites working-family tax credit.

abortion.summary: Voted against House Bill 1957, a proposed amendment that would add abortion-rights protections to the Pennsylvania Constitution, in a December 2025 House vote.
abortion.short: Voted against proposed state constitutional abortion-rights amendment.

education.summary: His campaign says he has worked to empower parents, rather than Harrisburg bureaucrats, with more control over their children's education.
education.short: Says he works to give parents more education control.

energy.summary: Supports Senate Bill 186 to withdraw Pennsylvania from the Regional Greenhouse Gas Initiative, saying government should get out of the way of the energy industry and that RGGI uncertainty has raised electricity rates and pushed energy investment to other states.
energy.short: Supports withdrawing Pennsylvania from RGGI carbon-pricing program.

guns.summary: Said protecting the Second Amendment right to keep and bear arms has always been important to him, and that he believes Article 1 Section 21 of the Pennsylvania Constitution protects an individual's freedom to own and possess firearms without government intrusion.
guns.short: Says constitution protects firearm ownership without government intrusion.
